shouldFix.title: The new AND invariant puts nineteen unresolved advisory dispositions in a ledger that its governing rule defines as repaired findings
evidence: honestyRepairsKeyRule begins: 'honestyRepairsFromVN lists findings raised against version N, repaired in a successor.' v16 changes the later coverage condition from register OR FromVN to register AND FromVN, making the repair ledger mandatory for every advisory.
A mechanical join of the v8-v15 register dispositions to the FromVN entry prefixes finds nineteen ids whose register disposition is ADVISORY-NON-BLOCKING but which now appear in honestyRepairsFromVN.

The contradiction is explicit in the current round. honestyRepairsFromV15 says HAE15-ADV-01 is registered while 'FC-SUBTYPE-CLASS still exercises no CA-3 row'; HAE15-ADV-02 says destinations.actionSubtype 'still mixes' vocabularies; HAE15-ADV-03 says coveredActs 'retains' its case variants. predecessorVerdictFindings.v15 labels each ADVISORY-NON-BLOCKING, not REPAIRED.

The same pattern is backfilled into earlier FromVN arrays: the newly added entries say only 'Registered ADVISORY-NON-BLOCKING'. Registering an advisory satisfies lineage completeness, but it does not repair the finding under the rule's own definition.

The actual register and frozen-review finding sets are exact after normalization, so this is not an omission or host-authorization blocker; it is a false governing classification introduced by the repair.
shouldFix.impact: A consumer cannot tell whether honestyRepairsFromVN means substantive repair or merely successor disposition. The governing sentence says the former while nineteen entries and their parallel register dispositions say the latter, so the lineage can falsely report standing observations as repaired.
shouldFix.requiredRepair: Keep every frozen finding in predecessorVerdictFindings, but require honestyRepairsFromVN only for register rows whose disposition is REPAIRED. Remove ADVISORY-NON-BLOCKING ids from the repair arrays. Alternatively replace the arrays and governing definition with a structured honestyDispositionsFromVN ledger whose entries distinguish REPAIRED from ADVISORY-NON-BLOCKING without calling both repairs.

shouldFix.title: registerCoverageRule's union-only comparison accepts wrong reviewer provenance and duplicate cross-lane findings
evidence: The new check compares one set union of claude2.findings and codex.findings to one union of both frozen verdicts. It never compares either reviewer lane to its own pinned verdict.

An in-memory counterexample swaps the complete v15 Claude and Codex findings arrays. The register union remains the same seven ids, so the stated check passes even though neither lane matches its frozen path and digest.

A second counterexample duplicates HAE15-CX-01 into the Claude lane while retaining it in Codex. Set union still equals the same seven frozen ids, so the check passes with eight registered lane/id pairs and only seven unique ids.

The right-hand extraction is also unspecified across the pinned corpus. Frozen Claude v8/v10/v12 use a combined findings[] array with integer blockers/shouldFix/advisories counters, while the other frozen reviews use severity arrays. The exact v8-v15 comparison passes only after applying an undocumented schema branch.

The actual v16 v15-register entry is correctly lane-assigned, duplicate-free, and complete. The defect is therefore in the standing rule claimed as mechanical enforcement, not in the current seven-id data, which bounds it to SHOULD-FIX rather than a blocker.
shouldFix.impact: The rule can certify a register whose per-reviewer provenance is false or duplicated, and independent implementations can extract different frozen finding sets. That leaves the successor-time guard vulnerable to the same lineage-accounting class it was introduced to prevent.
shouldFix.requiredRepair: Compare canonical (reviewerLane, findingId) pairs, or compare each lane separately to the findings extracted from that lane's pinned frozen verdict; require uniqueness and exact equality. Define the frozen-review extractor for both combined findings[] and severity-array schemas, and define canonical FromVN id extraction rather than relying on free-form string appearance.
